Definition: from a compound of the base of G297 and G906; a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish):--net.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea, for they were fishers. It is a casting net, thrown out over the water and drawn back in — the tool of their trade on the morning Jesus called them to follow Him.
TheologicalSignificance: One net in one verse carries no teaching of its own; its weight is the moment — two fishermen at work, and the call that turned them into fishers of men.
